digest.component_or_area: tracker initialization and environment identity management
propositions: Re-cloning the tracker without preserving git-ignored local state (.env-id, .opcert-key, .opcert-key.pub) silently mints a new environment identity, invalidating all prior attestations signed by the old one

Minting .env-id into a store already containing events from another environment must warn loudly on stderr, naming the prior env id(s), the attestation consequence, and the git-ignored files to carry over, but must still complete to allow legitimate multi-clone workflows
REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY=1 environment variable acknowledges the re-identification and quietens the warning to a one-line note
rebar fsck must emit a counted ENV_ID_MISMATCH issue when this environment's author also wrote events under a different env id, scoped to avoid false positives in healthy multi-clone topologies

The environment identity concern is extracted into a new leaf module src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py to handle read/mint, scanning for prior ids in events, override logic, warning text, the relocated env-id ensure unit, and fsck divergence reporting
docs/concurrency.md must document the re-clone carry-over list (.env-id, .opcert-key, .opcert-key.pub, .ensure-applied), what breaks per file, and why the guard warns rather than refuses
